title: GRACE ACS risque et mortalité calculateur
formula: Nomogramme, comme détaillé sous [8. Modèle de Fox pour le décès entre l’admission hospitalière et 6 mois plus tard](https://www.outcomes-umassmed.org/grace/files/GRACE_RiskModel_Coefficients.pdf).

how_to_use.why:
- This score is an extensively validated and guideline-endorsed tool for risk stratification in acute coronary syndromes.
- By combining readily available clinical, ECG, and laboratory data, it provides a reliable estimate of short- and long-term mortality, helping clinicians identify high-risk patients who benefit most from early invasive strategies and intensified medical therapy.
- Additionally, it supports meaningful prognostic discussions with patients and families, promotes standardized decision-making across providers, and aligns care with evidence-based recommendations.
- Consistent performance across large, diverse international cohorts makes the tool valuable for improving both clinical outcomes and communication in the care of ACS patients.
how_to_use.when:
- Appliquer aux patients présentant un ACS confirmé pour estimer le risque de mortalité, guider le choix du moment des stratégies invasives et étayer les discussions pronostiques.
- Ne doit pas être utilisé chez les patients présentant une douleur thoracique non différenciée avant que le diagnostic d’ACS ne soit posé.
how_to_use.pearls:
- This is a widely validated, guideline-endorsed prognostic model.
- GRACE 2.0 improves accuracy with non-linear modeling and extended (1–3 year) mortality predictions.
- Uses readily available clinical, ECG, and lab variables.
- Has strong discrimination across multiple populations (>20,000 patients in external validations).
- Helps guide timing of invasive strategies.
- Very useful for structured communication of risk with patients/families.
- Prognostic only and is not designed for diagnosing ACS or undifferentiated chest pain.
- Use of this tool should not delay time-sensitive reperfusion in STEMI.
- Calibration can drift over time or vary by setting; local validation/recalibration may be required.
- May over- or underestimate risk in elderly/frail patients; does not include frailty or comorbidity burden.
- Omits social determinants (e.g., socioeconomic deprivation) that might influence outcomes.
- Requires [Killip class](nabda:calc.killip-classification-heart-failure) and creatinine; missing or subjective inputs can affect accuracy.

next_steps.advice:
- Le score GRACE est un outil pronostique d'aide à la décision ; l'utiliser conjointement au jugement clinique, à l'ECG, à la troponine et à l'évaluation de la stabilité du patient.
- Discuter des résultats avec les patients et leurs proches afin de guider les attentes et les décisions partagées.
next_steps.critical_actions:
- Mortality estimate increases as the GRACE score increases.
- Results can be used as one factor in determining a course of care and may assist in communication with the patient about their risk; it should not be used in isolation when determining a treatment plan.
- Ensure high-risk patients have guideline-directed care during their hospitalization, as well as appropriate specialist and primary care follow-up upon discharge.
next_steps.management:
- The[ESC 2023](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37740496/)and[ACC/AHA 2025](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40014670/)acute coronary syndrome guidelines support the use of the GRACE score to identify high-risk patients with acute coronary syndrome for risk stratification to early invasive strategy (score >140).
- In patients with STEMI, results should not delay an invasive strategy but can be used to provide prognostic information.

evidence:
The GRACE 2.0 score is a well-validated, guideline-endorsed tool for risk stratification in acute coronary syndromes, with strong discrimination (area under the curve [AUC] ≈0.8) and clear clinical utility in guiding invasive strategy timing and prognostic discussions.

Derived from a large, multinational registry (n=21,688) and externally validated in diverse populations, it demonstrates broad applicability; however, calibration may drift over time and across healthcare systems, necessitating local validation and potential recalibration.

Strengths include clinical relevance, feasibility, and ease of use. Limitations include reliance on subjective inputs (e.g., [Killip class](nabda:calc.killip-classification-heart-failure) ), lack of frailty and socioeconomic factors, and possible over- or underestimation of risk in elderly or socioeconomically deprived groups.

Overall, GRACE 2.0 is a robust prognostic aid to inform management and communication in ACS, but it should always be used alongside clinical judgment, local validation, and consideration of patient context.
